items.text: The four ghosts by four-cycling, an explaining. Resolving the Hard Problem Registry seats each of its ten unchangeables at two of Exhibit ONE's numbers, its name with now and the same name eight up with next: an opening fixing as a place at 1 and 9, an observing fixing from behind at 2 and 10, a two-way fixing to one side at 3 and 11, a sequencing fixing to one beat at 4 and 12, a middle fixing as an end and a between fixing as a cut at 5 and 13, a completing fixing as a last at 6 and 14, a parity fixing as a magnitude and a rate fixing as a value at 7 and 15, a same-existing fixing as a store at 8 and 16. Four-cycling's four are Exhibit ONE's columns, 1, 5, 9, 13 next-existing, 2, 6, 10, 14 now-existing, 3, 7, 11, 15 prior-existing, 4, 8, 12, 16 same-existing. By the seatings a ghost at prior-existing is a rate, a magnitude or a side installed as a thing; at now-existing a first behind or a last; at next-existing a place, an end or a cut; at same-existing a store or a beat; and each ghost is one name at two seats, with now and with next. The four pair as Exhibit ONE's bi-foldings pair, next with same and now with prior. At a carbon chain, thirty-four of a registry's forty-four observings have an unchangeable with a seating, and each fixed thing is of the moment its seating gives, thirty-four of thirty-four: at prior with now a rate, a constant, an order, a first behind or a limit; at next with same a selection at a site, a cut, a boundary, a store or a code; each in one pairing and none in both.
